objects.description: Describes a view into interleaved float attribute buffers for Osd evaluators. Holds byte/element indices as integers: offset is the starting element index in the underlying array, length is the number of float components per element, and stride is the distance (in components) to the next element. Provides helpers to compute local offset within a stride, validate consistency, reset, and equality. Intended to be passed alongside device buffer objects to define sub-ranges/lanes of vertex attributes. All components are assumed to be floats per the API convention; destructor/ownership are trivial (POD). Unknowns: no alignment or byte-size semantics beyond element counts; no direct lifetime management.

        STENCIL_TABLE const *stencilTable,
        const CpuEvaluator *instance = NULL,
        void * deviceContext = NULL) {

        (void)instance;       // unused
        (void)deviceContext;  // unused

        return EvalStencils(srcBuffer->BindCpuBuffer(), srcDesc,

                            &stencilTable->GetSizes()[0],
                            &stencilTable->GetOffsets()[0],
                            &stencilTable->GetControlIndices()[0],
                            &stencilTable->GetWeights()[0],
                            /*start = */ 0,

objects.description: A stateless CPU-side evaluator utility in OpenSubdiv that provides static functions to evaluate Far stencil and patch tables on raw CPU buffers or buffer wrapper types. It supports computing values and first/second derivatives for vertex, varying, and face-varying data. All methods are static; there is no lifetime management or state.

CPU-side patch table wrapper used by Osd evaluators. It stages and exposes contiguous buffers of patch arrays, patch indices, and patch parameters, including variants for varying data and per-face-varying (fvar) channels. It is constructed from a Far::PatchTable and provides raw-pointer accessors to internal vectors. Destruction is trivial; lifetime management is manual (created with Create or constructor, delete when done). Internal element types PatchArray, PatchParam, PatchArrayVector, and PatchParamVector are declared elsewhere (included headers) and not defined here.

Concrete CPU-side vertex buffer implementing the Osd VertexBufferInterface. Holds an interleaved float array with numVertices vertices, each with numElements float components. Create() allocates the buffer; UpdateData() uploads a range from a client float array; BindCpuBuffer() returns a writable pointer to the internal CPU storage. Lifetime is managed by the caller; destructor frees internal storage. The optional deviceContext parameter is accepted for API compatibility but is unused on CPU.

enum MeshBits {
    MeshAdaptive             = 0,
    MeshInterleaveVarying    = 1,
    MeshFVarData             = 2,
    MeshFVarAdaptive         = 3,
    MeshUseSmoothCornerPatch = 4,
    MeshUseSingleCreasePatch = 5,
    MeshUseInfSharpPatch     = 6,
    MeshEndCapBilinearBasis  = 7,  // exclusive
    MeshEndCapBSplineBasis   = 8,  // exclusive
    MeshEndCapGregoryBasis   = 9,  // exclusive
    MeshEndCapLegacyGregory  = 10, // exclusive
    NUM_MESH_BITS            = 11,
};
objects.description: Bit indices used to configure mesh refinement and patch table generation behavior (adaptive/uniform refinement, varying layout, FVar handling, patch options, and end-cap basis selection). Values are indices for a bitset, not bit masks.

objects.definition: typedef std::bitset<NUM_MESH_BITS> MeshBitset;
objects.description: Type alias for a std::bitset sized to NUM_MESH_BITS, used to carry MeshBits flags when constructing and refining meshes.

Holds a reference to a specific patch (via Far::PatchTable::PatchHandle) and a 2D parametric coordinate (s, t) on that patch. Useful for locating points on the surface defined by a patch table. Construction is via its provided constructors; no special destruction semantics are indicated.

Describes a contiguous array of patches in index/parameter buffers, including their descriptor(s), count, base offsets, and stride. Two constructors allow single-type or mixed regular/irregular descriptors. No custom ownership; values reference external buffers by integer offsets.

Extends Far::PatchParam with an additional sharpness value for the patch. No constructors are provided here; default construction relies on Far::PatchParam’s behavior. Destruction is trivial. Details of Far::PatchParam fields are external to this header.

objects.definition: typedef std::vector<PatchArray> PatchArrayVector;
objects.description: Alias for a vector of Osd::PatchArray objects. Used to collect multiple patch arrays.

objects.definition: typedef std::vector<PatchParam> PatchParamVector;
objects.description: Alias for a vector of Osd::PatchParam objects. Used to store per-patch parameters associated with patch arrays.

C++ qualified name of OsdPatchParam when this header is compiled in C++ with namespaces enabled. The actual type definition is not present in this header; it is only referenced. This entry aliases the unqualified OsdPatchParam pointer for completeness.

objects.definition: class PatchTree;
objects.description: Forward declaration of the Bfr::PatchTree class, the (current) sole representation of irregular patches in Bfr. Only an incomplete type is provided here; its full definition is elsewhere.

objects.definition: typedef PatchTree IrregularPatchType;
objects.description: Internal alias type for the irregular patch representation. It is a typedef to Bfr::PatchTree, used to abstract the concrete implementation within internal code.

objects.definition: typedef std::shared_ptr<const IrregularPatchType> IrregularPatchSharedPtr;
objects.description: Internal shared-pointer typedef to a const IrregularPatchType (i.e., const Bfr::PatchTree). Facilitates shared ownership semantics for the irregular patch representation; note the pointed-to object is const.

Struct providing static query functions for topology-related limits within the Bfr component of OpenSubdiv. Offers MaxValence() and MaxFaceSize(), both returning Far::VALENCE_LIMIT. It contains no data members and is used as a namespace-like holder for constants. Construction is not required; methods are static. Note: the actual limit value comes from Far::VALENCE_LIMIT defined in far/types.h; details are external to this header.

Defines a face-local 2D (u,v) parameterization for a polygonal face given a subdivision scheme and face vertex count. Provides queries for type, face size, vertex/edge/center coordinates, and conversion utilities when the parameterization is partitioned into quadrilateral sub-faces (e.g., irregular faces under certain schemes). Construction is valid only via the constructor taking Sdc::SchemeType and face size; default construction yields an invalid object (IsValid() == false). The internal _type encodes the enum Type, _uDim holds the sub-face grid width when partitioned, and _faceSize is the face vertex count. Some template methods are declared but their definitions are not present in this header.
Enumeration of parameterization kinds: quadrilateral, triangular, or partitioned into quadrilateral sub-faces. Used by Parameterization to report its internal layout and conversion behavior.

Intermediate subclass of SurfaceFactory that adapts a Far::TopologyRefiner mesh to the SurfaceFactoryMeshAdapter interface. Provides queries for mesh, face counts, and fvar channels, and implements the virtual adapters for face/vertex/fvar topology and optional regular patch queries. Construction takes a TopologyRefiner and Options; destructor is defaulted. Details about caching are deferred to subclasses. Some types referenced (Index, FVarID, VertexDescriptor, Options, SurfaceFactory) are defined in included headers, not here.

objects.definition: class TopologyRefiner;
objects.description: Forward declaration of Far::TopologyRefiner. It is referenced as a const reference in RefinerSurfaceFactoryBase and RefinerSurfaceFactory but not defined in this header. Purpose: represents the connected mesh topology used by the surface factory.

Internal utility class encapsulating all state needed to build a Bfr Surface. Intended for use by SurfaceFactory; provides storage for control-vertex indices, parameterization, flags (valid/double/regular/linear), regular patch metadata, and an optional irregular patch reference. Lifetime: destructor calls invalidate(); construction details depend on external definitions not present here.

objects.definition: typedef int Index;
objects.description: Local alias within SurfaceData for control-vertex index type. Used for CV arrays and related accessors. Built-in base type is int; no additional semantics specified here.

objects.definition: typedef internal::IrregularPatchType      IrregPatchType;
objects.description: Local alias to internal::IrregularPatchType. The underlying type is declared elsewhere; here it is only aliased within SurfaceData for convenience when referring to irregular patch descriptions. Definition is external to this header.

objects.definition: typedef internal::IrregularPatchSharedPtr IrregPatchPtr;
objects.description: Local alias to a shared-pointer type for irregular patches. The concrete pointer/shared type is defined elsewhere; SurfaceData stores an instance to reference an irregular patch. Definition details not present here.

Abstract factory base class that initializes Bfr::Surface instances for mesh faces. It inherits SurfaceFactoryMeshAdapter to query mesh topology from a connected mesh. Subclasses provide mesh-specific connectivity via the adapter interface and use the protected constructor. Provides methods to query scheme/options, test for limit-surface existence, initialize Surfaces for vertex, varying, and face-varying data, and convenience creators. Manages caching via an external or internal SurfaceFactoryCache. Details of some collaborators are forward-declared in this header. Usage requires subclassing and supplying mesh connectivity. Construction/destruction behavior beyond virtual destructor is not specified here.

Simple configuration holder for SurfaceFactory instances. Controls default face-varying channel ID, caching enable/disable and external cache pointer, and approximation refinement levels used when approximating limit surfaces for smooth and sharp features. Lacks ownership semantics for the external cache pointer; lifetime management is unspecified here.

Abstract adapter interface that exposes a connected mesh to the SurfaceFactory. Subclasses must provide topology queries and index gathering for faces and face-vertices, plus optional fast paths for purely regular neighborhoods. It owns no state; all pure-virtual methods must be implemented by a concrete mesh wrapper. Construction/destruction are protected; use via subclassing. Inline defaults for the optional regular-fast-path methods return false.

objects.definition: typedef int Index;
objects.description: Integral mesh index type used throughout SurfaceFactoryMeshAdapter for faces, vertices, and face-varying value indices. It is an alias of int; -1 may be used to indicate boundary/missing entries in regular fast paths.

objects.definition: typedef std::intptr_t FVarID;
objects.description: Identifier type for selecting a particular set of face-varying primvars. It may be interpreted by the subclass as either an integer ID or a pointer-sized token.

objects.definition: class VertexDescriptor;
objects.description: Forward declaration only. Describes the topology and sharpness around a face-vertex used by SurfaceFactoryMeshAdapter::populateFaceVertexDescriptor. Definition is not present in this header.

Internal cache container used by Bfr::SurfaceFactory to store and reuse internal irregular patch representations. It manages a map from a 64-bit key to an internal::IrregularPatchSharedPtr. Copying is disabled; intended to be constructed and shared among factories. Provides virtual Find/Add hooks that subclasses can override (e.g., to add thread-safety) and non-virtual find/add helpers implementing the actual lookup/insert using the underlying map. Size() exposes the current number of cached entries. Construction/destruction details are not visible in this header; the exact semantics of DataType (lifecycle and ownership) depend on internal::IrregularPatchSharedPtr. Unknowns: exact key composition and eviction policy are not specified.

Class encapsulating a tessellation pattern for a given Bfr::Parameterization of a mesh face. It stores options, tessellation rates, inventory counts, and provides APIs to query/generate 2D parameter-space coordinates and facet index tuples, and to transform facet indices. Construction accepts either a single uniform rate or a vector of edge/inner rates. Copy and default construction are disabled; destructor declared. Details of actual tessellation generation are defined in the corresponding source file.

objects.description: Nested configuration class for Tessellation controlling quad preservation, facet size (3 or 4), and array strides for facets and (u,v) coordinates. Fluent setters return *this for chaining.

A non-publicly constructible helper class used by Bfr::SurfaceFactory subclasses to fully describe the topological neighborhood around a face corner vertex. It captures manifold/boundary flags, per-incident-face sizes, and optional vertex/edge creasing sharpness. Construction is controlled by Initialize/Finalize; validity can be queried. Instances are friend-accessed by FaceVertex and are intended to be stack or internal objects, not user-created. Details like constructor behavior and limits (e.g., 16-bit face counts) are implied by comments; exact constraints may require consulting implementation.

Describes and identifies the type of a subdivision patch in OpenSubdiv Far. Encapsulates a patch category via an enum (points, lines, quads, triangles, Loop, various Catmull-Clark/Gregory-based patches) and provides utilities to query whether it is adaptive and the number of expected control vertices. Stores the type as an unsigned int and offers comparison operators for ordering/equality. The class does not itself allocate external resources; construction is trivial. Details for GetAdaptivePatchDescriptors are declared here but defined elsewhere.

objects.definition:
enum Type {
        NON_PATCH = 0,     ///< undefined

        POINTS,            ///< points (useful for cage drawing)
        LINES,             ///< lines  (useful for cage drawing)

        QUADS,             ///< 4-sided quadrilateral (bilinear)
        TRIANGLES,         ///< 3-sided triangle

        LOOP,              ///< regular triangular patch for the Loop scheme

        REGULAR,           ///< regular B-Spline patch for the Catmark scheme
        GREGORY,
        GREGORY_BOUNDARY,
        GREGORY_BASIS,
        GREGORY_TRIANGLE
    };
objects.description: Scoped enumeration inside PatchDescriptor representing all supported patch kinds. Used with PatchDescriptor to compute control vertex counts and adaptivity. Underlying type is implementation-defined (int).

objects.definition: typedef Vtr::ConstArray<PatchDescriptor> ConstPatchDescriptorArray;
objects.description: Alias for an immutable contiguous array view of PatchDescriptor elements. The Vtr::ConstArray template is declared elsewhere; here we define a convenient typedef for arrays of PatchDescriptor used by APIs like GetAdaptivePatchDescriptors.

Encodes the parameterization metadata for a refined patch produced by topological subdivision. Stores packed bitfields for coarse face id, subdivision depth, u/v origin in a quadtree parameterization, boundary and transition edge masks, and flags for non-quad roots and regular patches. Provides helpers to normalize/unnormalize param coordinates and a variant for triangular patches including rotated-triangle handling. Construction is via Set(); storage is two 32-bit bitfield words. Destruction has no special requirements.

objects.description: Alias for a contiguous, dynamic sequence of PatchParam objects.

Quadtree-based lookup structure mapping a patch face ID and local (u,v) coordinates to a PatchTable::PatchHandle representing the sub-patch containing that parametric location. Constructed from a PatchTable; supports both quad and triangular patch layouts. Use FindPatch to retrieve a handle or null if unsupported/hole.

Primary container class representing a table of parametric patches produced by OpenSubdiv refinement. Provides accessors for patch arrays, per-patch data, varying and face-varying data, local point stencil tables, and basis evaluation utilities. Constructed internally by builders; copy-constructible and destructible. Ownership of internal stencil tables is not specified here.
Lightweight handle used as a unique identifier for a patch within a PatchTable. Holds indices into the patch arrays and into control-vertex storage. Members are public in this header for now.

Factory class that builds Far::PatchTable objects from a Far::TopologyRefiner, with configurable options for refinement, end-caps, precision, and table generation. Provides a static Create function and nests configuration and tag types.

Configuration struct for PatchTableFactory specifying end-cap basis, refinement isolation, precision for vertex and face-varying patches, and which auxiliary tables to generate. Provides helpers to map options to TopologyRefiner::AdaptiveOptions.
Enumeration of end-cap approximation bases used when creating irregular patches. Controls the basis type for end-caps during patch table creation.

Obsolete internal tag struct formerly used by the factory to inventory patch characteristics for allocation. Contains bitfields describing patch regularity, transitions, and boundary properties; methods are declared but defined elsewhere.

objects.definition: typedef std::vector<PatchFaceTag> PatchTagVector;
objects.description: Alias typedef for a vector of PatchFaceTag elements, used to collect per-face tags. Simple container type.
Concrete convenience typedef-class of PrimvarRefinerReal using float weights. Wraps a TopologyRefiner and exposes the same interpolation/limit API with REAL fixed to float.

A helper class that computes and queries the mapping between coarse mesh faces and Ptex face indices for a given TopologyRefiner. After construction with a refiner, it can report total Ptex face count, map a coarse face to its Ptex face id, and retrieve adjacency (neighbor Ptex faces and corresponding edges). Implementation details are not present in this header. Construction requires a TopologyRefiner; internal storage is a vector of Index values. Destruction is non-virtual and likely trivial.
Non-template convenience alias of StencilReal<float> for single stencil access with float weights.
Non-template float specialization wrapper for StencilTableReal, returning Stencil objects for convenience.
Non-template convenience alias of LimitStencilReal<float> for limit stencils with float weights and derivatives.
Non-template float specialization wrapper for LimitStencilTableReal, returning LimitStencil objects for convenience.

objects.description: Forward declaration only. A builder utility that can be a friend of stencil tables. Definition is not present in this header.

Non-template convenience wrapper that fixes REAL=float for StencilTableFactoryReal. Exposes Create and AppendLocalPoint* static methods returning the non-templated StencilTable pointer via reinterpret_cast.
Non-template convenience wrapper that fixes REAL=float for LimitStencilTableFactoryReal. Provides a Create method returning a LimitStencilTable pointer via reinterpret_cast.

Container of raw, read-only mesh-topology buffers used by TopologyRefinerFactory to build a TopologyRefiner. Holds counts for vertices/faces and pointers to arrays describing face-vertex incidence, creases, corners, holes, handedness, and optional face-varying channels. Fields are references; memory ownership and lifetime must be managed by the caller and outlive factory use. Constructor is declared here; definition is external.

Nested helper struct describing one face-varying (FVar) data channel for TopologyDescriptor. Specifies the number of unique FVar values and an array of value indices per face-vertex, aligned with the mesh's vertex indices for each face. Constructor zero-initializes fields.

A lightweight façade class providing read-only accessors into a single refinement level of an OpenSubdiv topology hierarchy. Instances are created and owned by TopologyRefiner and expose relationships, feature tags, face-varying channels, and parent/child linkage for that level. Lifetime is tied to the owning TopologyRefiner and underlying Vtr::internal::Level/Refinement objects.

Core class representing a topological mesh refiner in OpenSubdiv Far. It owns refinement levels and provides uniform and adaptive refinement, inventory of totals, and access to Far::TopologyLevel views. Construction requires a subdivision scheme type and options. Copy construction is protected and used via factory. Not default-constructible and not assignable. Destruction responsibilities for internal levels depend on _baseLevelOwned (details not present here).
Options POD for uniform refinement when calling TopologyRefiner::RefineUniform. Controls refinement level, vertex ordering, and whether to build full topology in the last level.
Options POD for feature-adaptive refinement when calling TopologyRefiner::RefineAdaptive. Controls isolation depth, feature handling, and vertex ordering.

Private base class for factories that construct Far::TopologyRefiner objects from client mesh representations. Provides protected helper hooks used by the templated factory to validate and prepare stages of construction. Not intended to be instantiated directly.

Explicit template specializations of several member functions for Sdc::Scheme instantiated with the SCHEME_BILINEAR tag. The header does not define the Scheme class itself nor the SCHEME_BILINEAR enumerant; it only specializes behavior (split type, regular sizes, and various mask assignment/limit functions) for the bilinear subdivision scheme.

Referenced as the return type of Scheme<SCHEME_CATMARK>::GetTopologicalSplitType(). The actual enum/type Split is not defined in this header; it is presumably defined in an included header (../sdc/scheme.h). Because it is not defined here, it should be ignored per the instructions.

A class template specialization of Scheme for the Catmull-Clark (Catmark) subdivision scheme. This header only provides inline specializations of member functions for SCHEME_CATMARK; the primary template, enum tag SCHEME_CATMARK, and related types (Options, EDGE/VERTEX/MASK concepts) are defined in other headers. The functions compute masks and limit masks/tangents used during subdivision. Construction and destruction details are unknown here.

Light-weight utility class in Sdc namespace for semi-sharp creasing computations, independent of subdivision scheme topology. Provides constants, helpers to classify sharpness, subdivision/decay of sharpness values, rule determination, and transitional weighting. Holds Options to control behavior. Construction/destruction are trivial; no ownership of external resources.
Enumeration of subdivision rule categories used at a vertex depending on sharpness configuration. Values are bit-flags enabling bitwise combination or testing across vertex sets.

A template specialization of Sdc::Scheme for SCHEME_LOOP providing Loop subdivision rules. This header defines only member function specializations (e.g., mask assignment and trait queries). The actual class template definition for Scheme<> and the SCHEME_LOOP enum value are declared elsewhere (included from ../sdc/scheme.h). As no full class or enum definition appears here, this entry notes the specialized type only by pointer type; details like fields/ownership are unknown.

Options aggregates all subdivision scheme options affecting the limit surface in OpenSubdiv Sdc. It stores four settings (vertex boundary interpolation, face-varying linear interpolation, creasing method, and triangle subdivision rule) in compact byte fields with trivial getters/setters. Default configuration is: VTX_BOUNDARY_NONE, FVAR_LINEAR_ALL, CREASE_UNIFORM, TRI_SUB_CATMARK.
Enumeration selecting how vertex boundary interpolation is applied during subdivision: none, edges only, or edges and corners.
Enumeration controlling linearization of face-varying (per-face-vertex) data across the mesh: from fully smooth to fully bilinear, with several boundary-focused variants.
Enumeration choosing the rule used to evaluate crease weights: Catmull-Clark uniform rule or Chaikin rule.
Enumeration selecting weighting for triangle subdivision when using the Catmark scheme: Catmark weights or smooth-triangle weights.

Enumeration of all subdivision schemes supported by OpenSubdiv: bilinear, Catmull-Clark (Catmark), and Loop. Used to select the core scheme for topology and rules throughout Sdc. No additional flags or values are defined here.

Enumeration of face-splitting strategies associated with a subdivision scheme. Quad splitting applies to Catmark and Bilinear; triangle splitting applies to Loop; a hybrid mode is reserved for future extension.

Traits helper for scheme-dependent properties, parameterized by SchemeType. Provides static queries for the face split type, regular face size, regular vertex valence, local neighborhood size, and a human-readable name. Only declarations are provided here; implementations are elsewhere. No instances are required; all members are static.

functions.name: OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Osd::BufferDescriptor::BufferDescriptor
functions.description: Default constructor. Initializes offset, length, and stride to 0, yielding an empty/invalid descriptor until populated. Use when you want to declare a descriptor and fill in fields later.
requirements: No arguments or preconditions.
Descriptor constructed this way is not valid for evaluation until its fields are set such that IsValid() returns true.

functions.name: OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Osd::BufferDescriptor::BufferDescriptor
functions.description: Value constructor. Initializes a buffer layout descriptor for interleaved float data with the given offset, length, and stride (in element units). Intended to describe a subrange within a per-vertex interleaved buffer (e.g., XYZ, RGBA).
requirements: Arguments are taken as-is; no internal validation is performed.
If a valid/usable descriptor is required by downstream APIs, choose values such that IsValid() returns true (i.e., length > 0 and length <= stride - GetLocalOffset()).
Values represent counts/indices in elements, not bytes, and assume elements are floats as per the surrounding documentation.

functions.name: OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Osd::BufferDescriptor::GetLocalOffset
functions.description: Returns the offset of this attribute within a single stride (i.e., offset modulo stride). If stride <= 0, returns 0. Useful when computing placement of the attribute inside each interleaved element.
requirements: No preconditions; safe for any field values.
If stride <= 0, the function returns 0 by definition in this implementation.

functions.name: OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Osd::BufferDescriptor::IsValid
functions.description: Checks internal consistency of the descriptor. Returns true when length > 0 and length <= (stride - GetLocalOffset()). Indicates the described attribute fits within each interleaved element.
requirements: No preconditions; evaluates current field values.
Callers relying on a valid descriptor should check this result before using the descriptor with evaluator APIs.

functions.name: OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Osd::BufferDescriptor::Reset
functions.description: Resets the descriptor to its default state by setting offset, length, and stride to 0.
requirements: No preconditions.
After reset, the descriptor is not valid until fields are reassigned to values that make IsValid() return true.

functions.name: OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Osd::BufferDescriptor::operator==
functions.description: Equality operator. Returns true if offset, length, and stride are all equal to those of the other descriptor.
requirements: The referenced other descriptor must be a valid object.
No additional preconditions; comparison is value-based on the three fields.

functions.name: OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Osd::BufferDescriptor::operator!=
functions.description: Inequality operator. Returns true if any of offset, length, or stride differ from those of the other descriptor.
requirements: The referenced other descriptor must be a valid object.
No additional preconditions; comparison is value-based on the three fields.

functions.name: OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Osd::CpuEvaluator::EvalStencils
functions.signature:
template <typename SRC_BUFFER, typename DST_BUFFER, typename STENCIL_TABLE>
static bool OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Osd::CpuEvaluator::EvalStencils(
    SRC_BUFFER* srcBuffer, OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Osd::BufferDescriptor const& srcDesc,
    DST_BUFFER* dstBuffer, OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Osd::BufferDescriptor const& dstDesc,
    STENCIL_TABLE const* stencilTable,
    OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Osd::CpuEvaluator const* instance = NULL,
    void* deviceContext = NULL)
functions.description: Evaluates primvar stencils on CPU using buffer objects. Intended to mirror device-kernel interfaces so it can be called uniformly from OsdMesh. Reads from srcBuffer and writes results to dstBuffer using the given stencilTable over all its stencils.
requirements: SRC_BUFFER must provide const float* BindCpuBuffer() for read.
DST_BUFFER must provide float* BindCpuBuffer() for write.
stencilTable must supply methods GetNumStencils(), GetSizes(), GetOffsets(), GetControlIndices(), GetWeights().
If stencilTable->GetNumStencils() == 0, the function returns false and performs no work.
srcDesc and dstDesc describe layout; offsets in the descriptors are applied internally (do not pre-offset the bound pointers).
instance and deviceContext are unused and may be NULL.

functions.name: OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Osd::CpuEvaluator::EvalPatches
functions.signature:
template <typename SRC_BUFFER, typename DST_BUFFER, typename PATCHCOORD_BUFFER, typename PATCH_TABLE>
static bool OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Osd::CpuEvaluator::EvalPatches(
    SRC_BUFFER* srcBuffer, OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Osd::BufferDescriptor const& srcDesc,
    DST_BUFFER* dstBuffer, OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Osd::BufferDescriptor const& dstDesc,
    int numPatchCoords,
    PATCHCOORD_BUFFER* patchCoords,
    PATCH_TABLE* patchTable,
    OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Osd::CpuEvaluator const* instance = NULL,
    void* deviceContext = NULL)
functions.description: Evaluates limit positions at the specified patch coordinates using buffer objects and a patch table. Mirrors device-kernel interface and writes values to dstBuffer.
requirements: SRC_BUFFER must provide const float* BindCpuBuffer().
DST_BUFFER must provide float* BindCpuBuffer().
PATCHCOORD_BUFFER must provide a buffer whose BindCpuBuffer() can be cast to const PatchCoord*.
PATCH_TABLE must provide GetPatchArrayBuffer(), GetPatchIndexBuffer(), GetPatchParamBuffer().
numPatchCoords is the number of PatchCoord entries to evaluate and must match the patchCoords content length.
Descriptor offsets are applied internally to the bound src/dst pointers.
instance and deviceContext are unused.

numPatchCoords must match the number of PatchCoord entries given in patchCoords.
Descriptor offsets are applied internally.
instance and deviceContext are unused.

Descriptor offsets are applied internally.
instance and deviceContext are unused.

functions.name: OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Osd::OsdPatchParamGetParamFraction
functions.description: Computes and returns the parametric fraction for the patch as 1.0f / (1 << (depth - nonQuadRoot)), where depth and nonQuadRoot are derived from param. Used to scale between absolute and local patch UV domains.
requirements: param must be a valid OsdPatchParam.
Callers must ensure depth >= nonQuadRoot so the shift count (depth - nonQuadRoot) is non-negative; otherwise the left shift is undefined and may crash.
Given the encoding, depth is 0..15 and nonQuadRoot is 0 or 1; the resulting fraction must be positive and non-zero for valid params.

functions.name: OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Osd::OsdPatchParamIsRegular

requirements: param must be a valid OsdPatchParam.

functions.name: OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Osd::OsdPatchParamNormalize
functions.description: Normalizes the input uv from the absolute (global/tiled) domain into the local [0,1] patch domain using param. The operation is in-place on uv.
requirements: param must be a valid OsdPatchParam.
uv must point to a writable array of at least 2 floats.
OsdPatchParamGetParamFraction(param) must be positive and finite (see depth >= nonQuadRoot) to avoid division by zero or infinities.
On non-triangular patches this is the standard normalization; for triangles with rotation, use OsdPatchParamNormalizeTriangle instead.

functions.name: OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Osd::OsdPatchParamUnnormalize
functions.description: Unnormalizes the input uv from the local [0,1] patch domain back to the absolute (global/tiled) domain using param. The operation is in-place on uv.
requirements: param must be a valid OsdPatchParam.
uv must point to a writable array of at least 2 floats.
OsdPatchParamGetParamFraction(param) must be positive and finite to avoid generating NaNs or infinities.
For triangles with rotation semantics, use OsdPatchParamUnnormalizeTriangle instead.

functions.name: OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Osd::OsdPatchParamNormalizeTriangle
functions.description: Normalizes uv for triangular patches, accounting for potential rotation. If the triangle is rotated, applies a mirrored transform; otherwise falls back to OsdPatchParamNormalize. Operates in-place.
requirements: param must be a valid OsdPatchParam.
uv must point to a writable array of at least 2 floats.
OsdPatchParamGetParamFraction(param) must be positive and finite (requires depth >= nonQuadRoot) to avoid division by zero.
Intended for triangular patches; using on quads is harmless but unnecessary.

functions.name: OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Osd::OsdPatchParamUnnormalizeTriangle
functions.description: Unnormalizes uv for triangular patches, accounting for potential rotation. If rotated, applies the inverse mirrored transform; otherwise falls back to OsdPatchParamUnnormalize. Operates in-place.
requirements: param must be a valid OsdPatchParam.
uv must point to a writable array of at least 2 floats.
OsdPatchParamGetParamFraction(param) must be positive and finite (requires depth >= nonQuadRoot).
Intended for triangular patches; using on quads is harmless but unnecessary.

functions.name: OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Osd::OsdEvaluatePatchBasisNormalized
functions.signature: OSD_FUNCTION_STORAGE_CLASS int OsdEvaluatePatchBasisNormalized(int patchType, OsdPatchParam param, OSD_REAL s, OSD_REAL t, OSD_OUT_ARRAY(OSD_REAL, wP, 20), OSD_OUT_ARRAY(OSD_REAL, wDs, 20), OSD_OUT_ARRAY(OSD_REAL, wDt, 20), OSD_OUT_ARRAY(OSD_REAL, wDss, 20), OSD_OUT_ARRAY(OSD_REAL, wDst, 20), OSD_OUT_ARRAY(OSD_REAL, wDtt, 20))
functions.description: Evaluates basis weights and optionally derivatives for a patch specified by patchType at normalized parameters (s,t). Handles boundary adjustments for regular (B-spline) and Loop (box-spline) patches via param’s boundary mask. Writes results into arrays sized for the maximum point count (up to 20). Returns the number of points used by the selected patch type.
requirements: patchType must be one of: OSD_PATCH_DESCRIPTOR_REGULAR, OSD_PATCH_DESCRIPTOR_LOOP, OSD_PATCH_DESCRIPTOR_GREGORY_BASIS, OSD_PATCH_DESCRIPTOR_GREGORY_TRIANGLE, OSD_PATCH_DESCRIPTOR_QUADS, or OSD_PATCH_DESCRIPTOR_TRIANGLES.
param must be a valid OsdPatchParam; boundary is obtained via OsdPatchParamGetBoundary(param).
wP, if non-null, must reference an array with at least 20 elements; derivative arrays likewise must have at least 20 elements if requested.
For REGULAR and LOOP patch types, boundary adjustments are applied when boundary mask != 0.
Returns the number of weights for the chosen patch type: 16 (regular), 12 (loop), 20 (Gregory basis), 18 (Gregory triangle), 4 (quads), 3 (triangles).

functions.name: OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Osd::OsdEvaluatePatchBasis
functions.signature: OSD_FUNCTION_STORAGE_CLASS int OsdEvaluatePatchBasis(int patchType, OsdPatchParam param, OSD_REAL s, OSD_REAL t, OSD_OUT_ARRAY(OSD_REAL, wP, 20), OSD_OUT_ARRAY(OSD_REAL, wDs, 20), OSD_OUT_ARRAY(OSD_REAL, wDt, 20), OSD_OUT_ARRAY(OSD_REAL, wDss, 20), OSD_OUT_ARRAY(OSD_REAL, wDst, 20), OSD_OUT_ARRAY(OSD_REAL, wDtt, 20))
functions.description: High-level evaluator that normalizes parameters using OsdPatchParam and handles triangle orientation. Calls OsdEvaluatePatchBasisNormalized to compute weights. Scales derivatives by 2^depth and adjusts sign for rotated triangles. Returns the number of points for the selected patch type.
requirements: patchType must be one of the supported descriptors as in OsdEvaluatePatchBasisNormalized.
param must be a valid OsdPatchParam; parameter normalization is performed via OsdPatchParamNormalize/OsdPatchParamNormalizeTriangle and depth obtained via OsdPatchParamGetDepth(param).
Input (s,t) are raw patch-local parameters; they will be normalized internally based on param.
wP, if non-null, must reference an array with at least 20 elements; derivative arrays likewise must have at least 20 elements if requested.
If wDs and wDt are requested, both must be non-null. If second derivatives are requested, all three of wDss, wDst, wDtt must be non-null.
First derivatives are scaled by derivSign * 2^depth; second derivatives are scaled by derivSign * (2^depth)^2, where derivSign = -1 for rotated triangles and +1 otherwise.

functions.description: Writes the (u,v) parameter coordinates of the face center into uvCoord.

Only meaningful when HasSubFaces() is true; otherwise the return value is 0 by definition (explicit from implementation and comments).

requirements: HasSubFaces() should be true; only applicable for parameterizations with sub-faces (explicit).
subFace must be a valid sub-face index for this parameterization (inferred).

functions.description: Virtual destructor for RefinerSurfaceFactoryBase. Performs default cleanup; no additional behavior is specified in this header.

requirements: The RefinerSurfaceFactoryBase instance must be valid (constructed and not yet destroyed).

functions.name: OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Bfr::RefinerSurfaceFactory<>::RefinerSurfaceFactory
functions.signature:
template <class CACHE_TYPE = OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Bfr::SurfaceFactoryCache>
OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Bfr::RefinerSurfaceFactory<CACHE_TYPE>::RefinerSurfaceFactory(OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Far::TopologyRefiner const & mesh, OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Bfr::SurfaceFactory::Options const & options = OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Bfr::SurfaceFactory::Options())

mesh must be a valid OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Far::TopologyRefiner instance.

options may be omitted to use default-constructed Bfr::SurfaceFactory::Options.

functions.name: OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Bfr::RefinerSurfaceFactory<>::~RefinerSurfaceFactory
functions.description: Destructor for the concrete RefinerSurfaceFactory template. Performs default cleanup; the internal cache member is destroyed with the factory.
requirements: The object must have been constructed before being destroyed.
No additional cleanup requirements are specified in this header.

functions.name: OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Bfr::Surface::IsValid
functions.description: Returns whether this Surface instance has been successfully initialized by a SurfaceFactory and is usable for queries/evaluation.
requirements: The Surface object must have been initialized by a compatible SurfaceFactory to return true; otherwise it remains invalid after default construction or failed initialization.

functions.name: OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Bfr::Surface::Clear
functions.description: Clears any previously initialized internal state so the Surface becomes invalid and can be re-initialized by a SurfaceFactory.
requirements: After calling Clear(), IsValid() will return false until re-initialized.
Do not call evaluation or data access methods that require validity until the Surface is re-initialized.

functions.name: OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Bfr::Surface::Surface
functions.description: Default constructor. Produces an invalid Surface that must be initialized by a SurfaceFactory before use.
requirements: Must call a SurfaceFactory initializer before calling methods that require a valid Surface (e.g., evaluation, control/patch point access).

functions.name: OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Bfr::Surface::GetParameterization
functions.description: Returns the Parameterization associated with this Surface, which defines its (u,v) domain and face size.
requirements: Surface should be valid; otherwise contents of the returned Parameterization may not be meaningful (not specified).

functions.name: OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Bfr::Surface::GetFaceSize
functions.description: Returns the size (number of vertices) of the face associated with this Surface via its Parameterization.
requirements: None beyond standard object validity; derived from GetParameterization().

functions.name: OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Bfr::Surface::IsRegular
functions.description: Returns whether the Surface corresponds to a single regular patch.
requirements: The Surface should be valid for the result to be meaningful.

functions.name: OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Bfr::Surface::IsLinear
functions.description: Returns whether the Surface is linear (e.g., multi-linear case).
requirements: The Surface should be valid for the result to be meaningful.

functions.name: OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Bfr::Surface::GetNumControlPoints
functions.description: Returns the number of control points that affect this Surface.
requirements: Surface should be valid; count is defined by the initialized Surface data.

functions.name: OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Bfr::Surface::GetControlPointIndices
functions.description: Writes the mesh indices of the control points that influence this Surface into the provided array and returns the number written.
requirements: Surface must be valid.
meshPointIndices must point to writable, contiguous storage with capacity for at least GetNumControlPoints() entries.
Returned integer is the number of indices written (expected to be GetNumControlPoints()).

functions.name: OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Bfr::Surface::GatherControlPoints
functions.signature: template <typename REAL, typename REAL_MESH> void OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Bfr::Surface<REAL>::GatherControlPoints(REAL_MESH const meshPoints[], typename OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Bfr::Surface<REAL>::PointDescriptor const & meshPointDesc, REAL controlPoints[], typename OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Bfr::Surface<REAL>::PointDescriptor const & controlPointDesc) const
functions.description: Gathers the control points that influence this Surface from a contiguous mesh point array into a local control point array, converting precision if needed.
requirements: Surface must be valid.
meshPoints must reference a contiguous array of mesh point data; fragmented/paged data is not supported by this method.
meshPointDesc.size specifies the per-point dimension; meshPointDesc.stride specifies the stride in the mesh array; they must match the layout of meshPoints.
controlPoints must be a writable array large enough to hold GetNumControlPoints() points with controlPointDesc.stride and controlPointDesc.size layout.
controlPointDesc.size must match the desired per-point dimension of controlPoints.
Both descriptors’ size/stride must be positive and consistent with the allocated arrays (implied by usage).

functions.name: OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Bfr::Surface::BoundControlPoints
functions.signature: template <typename REAL> void OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Bfr::Surface<REAL>::BoundControlPoints(REAL const controlPoints[], typename OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Bfr::Surface<REAL>::PointDescriptor const & controlPointDesc, REAL minExtent[], REAL maxExtent[]) const
functions.description: Computes axis-aligned bounds of the control points provided in a local array and writes the minimum and maximum extents per component.
requirements: Surface must be valid.
controlPoints must contain the control points for this Surface laid out contiguously according to controlPointDesc.
controlPointDesc.size defines the number of components per point; minExtent and maxExtent arrays must each have capacity of at least controlPointDesc.size.
controlPointDesc.stride must correctly describe the memory layout of controlPoints.

functions.name: OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Bfr::Surface::BoundControlPointsFromMesh
functions.signature: template <typename REAL> void OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Bfr::Surface<REAL>::BoundControlPointsFromMesh(REAL const meshPoints[], typename OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Bfr::Surface<REAL>::PointDescriptor const & meshPointDesc, REAL minExtent[], REAL maxExtent[]) const
functions.description: Computes axis-aligned bounds of the Surface’s control points by reading them directly from a contiguous mesh point array.
requirements: Surface must be valid.
meshPoints must be a contiguous array; fragmented/paged mesh data is not supported by this method.
meshPointDesc.size defines the number of components per point; minExtent and maxExtent arrays must each have capacity of at least meshPointDesc.size.
meshPointDesc.stride must correctly describe the memory layout of meshPoints.

functions.name: OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Bfr::Surface::GetNumPatchPoints
functions.description: Returns the number of patch points required to represent this Surface for evaluation. Patch points include all control points plus any additional derived points.
requirements: Surface must be valid.

functions.name: OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Bfr::Surface::PreparePatchPoints
functions.signature: template <typename REAL> void OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Bfr::Surface<REAL>::PreparePatchPoints(REAL const meshPoints[], typename OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Bfr::Surface<REAL>::PointDescriptor const & meshPointDesc, REAL patchPoints[], typename OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Bfr::Surface<REAL>::PointDescriptor const & patchPointDesc) const
functions.description: Fills the provided patchPoints array with all patch points required for evaluation by first gathering control points from the contiguous mesh array and then computing any additional patch points.
requirements: Surface must be valid.
meshPoints must be contiguous; if mesh data is fragmented, first gather control points explicitly using GatherControlPoints, then call ComputePatchPoints.
meshPointDesc must correctly describe meshPoints layout.
patchPoints must be writable and large enough for GetNumPatchPoints() points with the given patchPointDesc layout.
patchPointDesc.size and stride must correctly describe the layout of patchPoints.

functions.name: OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Bfr::Surface::ComputePatchPoints
functions.signature: template <typename REAL> void OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Bfr::Surface<REAL>::ComputePatchPoints(REAL patchPoints[], typename OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Bfr::Surface<REAL>::PointDescriptor const & patchPointDesc) const
functions.description: Computes the derived patch points (beyond the control points) in-place in the provided patchPoints array. If the Surface is regular, no additional points are computed; otherwise linear or irregular points are computed as needed.
requirements: Surface must be valid.
The first GetNumControlPoints() points of patchPoints must already contain this Surface’s control points laid out per patchPointDesc.
patchPoints must have capacity for the full set of patch points: GetNumPatchPoints().
patchPointDesc.size/stride must match the layout of patchPoints.

functions.name: OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Bfr::Surface::Evaluate
functions.signature: template <typename REAL> void OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Bfr::Surface<REAL>::Evaluate(REAL const uv[2], REAL const patchPoints[], typename OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Bfr::Surface<REAL>::PointDescriptor const & pointDesc, REAL P[]) const
functions.description: Evaluates the Surface position at the given (u,v) and writes the result into P, using the provided patch points.
requirements: Surface must be valid.
uv must be within the domain defined by GetParameterization().
patchPoints must contain all patch points for this Surface laid out per pointDesc (size/stride), with capacity for GetNumPatchPoints() points.
P must be writable with capacity at least pointDesc.size components.

functions.name: OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Bfr::Surface::Evaluate
functions.signature: template <typename REAL> void OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Bfr::Surface<REAL>::Evaluate(REAL const uv[2], REAL const patchPoints[], typename OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Bfr::Surface<REAL>::PointDescriptor const & pointDesc, REAL P[], REAL Du[], REAL Dv[]) const
functions.description: Evaluates the Surface position and first derivatives with respect to u and v at (u,v). Writes results into P, Du, and Dv.
requirements: Surface must be valid.
uv must be within the domain defined by GetParameterization().
patchPoints must contain all patch points laid out per pointDesc.
P, Du, and Dv must each be writable arrays with capacity at least pointDesc.size components.

functions.name: OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Bfr::Surface::Evaluate
functions.signature: template <typename REAL> void OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Bfr::Surface<REAL>::Evaluate(REAL const uv[2], REAL const patchPoints[], typename OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Bfr::Surface<REAL>::PointDescriptor const & pointDesc, REAL P[], REAL Du[], REAL Dv[], REAL Duu[], REAL Duv[], REAL Dvv[]) const
functions.description: Evaluates the Surface position, first derivatives, and second derivatives at (u,v). Writes results into P, Du, Dv, Duu, Duv, and Dvv.
requirements: Surface must be valid.
uv must be within the domain defined by GetParameterization().
patchPoints must contain all patch points laid out per pointDesc.
All output arrays (P, Du, Dv, Duu, Duv, Dvv) must be writable with capacity at least pointDesc.size components.

functions.name: OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Bfr::Surface::EvaluateStencil
functions.signature: template <typename REAL> int OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Bfr::Surface<REAL>::EvaluateStencil(REAL const uv[2], REAL sP[]) const
functions.description: Computes the limit stencil coefficients for position at (u,v) with respect to the control points. Returns the number of control points (length of the stencil).
requirements: Surface must be valid.
uv must be within the domain defined by GetParameterization().
sP must be writable with capacity for at least GetNumControlPoints() coefficients.
The returned int is the number of coefficients written (expected to equal GetNumControlPoints()).

functions.name: OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Bfr::Surface::EvaluateStencil
functions.signature: template <typename REAL> int OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Bfr::Surface<REAL>::EvaluateStencil(REAL const uv[2], REAL sP[], REAL sDu[], REAL sDv[]) const
functions.description: Computes limit stencil coefficients at (u,v) for position and first derivatives with respect to the control points. Returns the number of control points (length of each stencil).
requirements: Surface must be valid.
uv must be within the domain defined by GetParameterization().
sP, sDu, and sDv must each be writable arrays with capacity for at least GetNumControlPoints() coefficients.
The returned int is the number of coefficients written (expected to equal GetNumControlPoints()).

functions.name: OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Bfr::Surface::EvaluateStencil
functions.signature: template <typename REAL> int OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Bfr::Surface<REAL>::EvaluateStencil(REAL const uv[2], REAL sP[], REAL sDu[], REAL sDv[], REAL sDuu[], REAL sDuv[], REAL sDvv[]) const
functions.description: Computes limit stencil coefficients at (u,v) for position, first derivatives, and second derivatives with respect to the control points. Returns the number of control points (length of each stencil).
requirements: Surface must be valid.
uv must be within the domain defined by GetParameterization().
All output arrays (sP, sDu, sDv, sDuu, sDuv, sDvv) must be writable with capacity for at least GetNumControlPoints() coefficients each.
The returned int is the number of coefficients written (expected to equal GetNumControlPoints()).

functions.name: OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Bfr::Surface::ApplyStencil
functions.signature: template <typename REAL> void OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Bfr::Surface<REAL>::ApplyStencil(REAL const stencil[], REAL const controlPoints[], typename OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Bfr::Surface<REAL>::PointDescriptor const &, REAL result[]) const
functions.description: Applies a single stencil to the provided controlPoints array to compute a single result value (e.g., position or derivative vector), independent of which derivative the stencil represents.
requirements: Surface must be valid.
stencil must contain coefficients corresponding to this Surface’s control points (length should match GetNumControlPoints()).
controlPoints must contain this Surface’s control points laid out contiguously per the provided PointDescriptor (size/stride).
result must be writable with capacity at least the descriptor size (number of components).

functions.name: OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Bfr::Surface::ApplyStencilFromMesh
functions.signature: template <typename REAL> void OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Bfr::Surface<REAL>::ApplyStencilFromMesh(REAL const stencil[], REAL const meshPoints[], typename OpenSubdiv::OPENSUBDIV_VERSION::Bfr::Surface<REAL>::PointDescriptor const &, REAL result[]) const
functions.description: Applies a single stencil directly to control points read from a contiguous mesh point array to compute a single result value.
requirements: Surface must be valid.
stencil must contain coefficients corresponding to this Surface’s control points (length should match GetNumControlPoints()).
meshPoints must be a contiguous array; the descriptor must correctly specify component size and stride.
result must be writable with capacity at least the descriptor size (number of components).
